![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14185522/assets/56b286d9b7c503c84891ebdf410797f715844eb8de344f71dc2fc652cbf3b5ef.png)

In the triangle above, what is the length of $\overset{―}{AC}?$
q-53474.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14185522/assets/85f119cdc6b7a80dd7cd4ea2a2a235e80723b7c2fe6837fa127beb8fd994d7ea.png)

Since this is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the shorter leg has length $x=3$ and the longer leg has length $\sqrt{3}x,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}AC=\sqrt{3}x=\sqrt{3}\cdot 3=3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the longer leg is $3\sqrt{3}.$

q-119567.worked_solution:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14185522/assets/b8f2ba89d30a41072f635916eb07b394fd4bd83eb39181f13e852d1b776de5ee.png)

Since this is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the longer leg has length $7\sqrt{3},$ and the shorter leg has length $x,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}7\sqrt{3} & =\sqrt{3}x \\ x & =\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the shorter leg is $7.$

q-119569.name: Question 3
q-119569.problem: What is the length of the side opposite the ${30}^{∘}$ angle in a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle if the side opposite the ${60}^{∘}$ angle has a length of $21?$
q-119569.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14185522/assets/1f7084b210e13a9c2753c3ae8bfcc9302b109cc9584f589c6b8937536ae93682.png)

  

Since this is a ${30}^{∘}$-${60}^{∘}$-${90}^{∘}$ triangle, the length of the longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the longer leg has length $21,$ and the shorter leg has length $x,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}21 & =\sqrt{3}x \\ x & =\frac{21}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical from the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and denominator by the radical:

$$
x=\frac{21}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{21\cdot \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{3}}=\frac{21\sqrt{3}}{3}=7\sqrt{3}
$$

So, the length of the shorter leg is $7\sqrt{3}.$

Question 3

a
3
b
7
c
73
d
37
e
21

Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's refer to our standard 30∘-60∘-90∘ triangle.

Since this is a 30∘-60∘-90∘ triangle, the length of the longer leg is 3 times that of the shorter leg.

Here, the longer leg has length 21, and the shorter leg has length x, so we have

21=3xx=213.

To remove the radical from the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and denominator by the radical:

x=213=21⋅33⋅3=2133=73

So, the length of the shorter leg is 73.
